sanskrit: brahmayonir mahān āsīt kuśo nāma mahātapāḥ vaidarbhyāṃ janayām āsa caturaḥ sadṛśān sutān kuśāmbaṃ kuśanābhaṃ ca ādhūrtarajasaṃ vasum
english: There was a great sage born of Brahmā, named Kuśa, a man of immense austerity. In Vaidarbhī he begot four sons alike in their qualities: Kuśāmba, Kuśanābha, Ādhūrtarajasa, and Vasu.

sanskrit: dīptiyuktān mahotsāhān kṣatradharmacikīrṣayā tān uvāca kuśaḥ putrān dharmiṣṭhān satyavādinaḥ kriyatāṃ pālanaṃ putrā dharmaṃ prāpsyatha puṣkalam
english: Radiant and supremely energetic, eager to fulfill the duties of kṣatriyas, Kuśa addressed those sons of his who were righteous and truthful: 'Rule over your subjects, O sons; thus you shall attain the fullness of dharma.'

sanskrit: kuśasya vacanaṃ śrutvā catvāro lokasaṃmatāḥ niveśaṃ cakrire sarve purāṇāṃ nṛvarās tadā
english: Hearing the words of Kuśa, those four foremost of kings, esteemed throughout the world, thereupon each established his own city.

sanskrit: kuśāmbas tu mahātejāḥ kauśāmbīm akarot purīm kuśanābhas tu dharmātmā paraṃ cakre mahodayam
english: The greatly resplendent Kuśāmba built the city of Kauśāmbī; the righteous Kuśanābha established the great city of Mahodaya.

sanskrit: ādhūrtarajaso rāma dharmāraṇyaṃ mahīpatiḥ cakre puravaraṃ rājā vasuś cakre girivrajam
english: O Rāma, Ādhūrtarajasa, that lord of the earth, built the excellent city of Dharmāraṇya; and King Vasu built Girivrajam.

sanskrit: eṣā vasumatī rāma vasos tasya mahātmanaḥ ete śailavarāḥ pañca prakāśante samantataḥ
english: This, O Rāma, is the land of that great-souled Vasu; and these five chief mountains shine forth on all sides.

sanskrit: sumāgadhī nadī ramyā māgadhān viśrutāyayau pañcānāṃ śailamukhyānāṃ madhye māleva śobhate
english: The lovely river Śumāgadhī, renowned among the Māgadhas, flows through; amidst those five great mountains she gleams like a garland.

sanskrit: saiṣā hi māgadhī rāma vasos tasya mahātmanaḥ pūrvābhicaritā rāma sukṣetrā sasyamālinī
english: This, O Rāma, is the Māgadhī river, traversed of old by that great-souled Vasu—a region of fair fields, garlanded with crops.

sanskrit: kuśanābhas tu rājarṣiḥ kanyāśatam anuttamam janayām āsa dharmātmā ghṛtācyāṃ raghunandana
english: The royal sage Kuśanābha, righteous of soul, begot in Ghṛtācī a hundred peerless daughters, O joy of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: tās tu yauvanaśālinyo rūpavatyaḥ svalaṃkṛtāḥ udyānabhūmim āgamya prāvṛṣīva śatahradāḥ
english: Those daughters, in the bloom of youth, beautiful and well adorned, came to the pleasure garden, like a hundred lightning flashes of the rainy season.

sanskrit: gāyantyo nṛtyamānāś ca vādayantyaś ca rāghava āmodaṃ paramaṃ jagmur varābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ
english: Singing, dancing, and playing instruments, O Rāghava, adorned with the finest ornaments, they gave themselves over to supreme delight.

sanskrit: atha tāś cārusarvāṅgyo rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi udyānabhūmim āgamya tārā iva ghanāntare
english: Those women, graceful in every limb and matchless in beauty upon earth, coming into the garden, shone like stars amid the clouds.

sanskrit: tāḥ sarvaguṇasaṃpannā rūpayauvanasaṃyutāḥ dṛṣṭvā sarvātmako vāyur idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing them endowed with every virtue and graced with beauty and youth, Vāyu, the all-pervading wind god, spoke these words.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vaḥ kāmaye sarvā bhāryā mama bhaviṣyatha mānuṣas tyajyatāṃ bhāvo dīrgham āyur avāpsyatha
english: 'I desire you all; you shall become my wives. Abandon your human condition and you shall attain long life.'

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vāyor akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ apahāsya tato vākyaṃ kanyāśatam athābravīt
english: Hearing those words of Vāyu, the tireless one, the hundred maidens laughed them off and then replied.

sanskrit: antaś carasi bhūtānāṃ sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ surottama prabhāvajñāś ca te sarvāḥ kim asmān avamanyase
english: 'You move within all beings, O best among gods; we all know your power. Why then do you treat us with contempt?'

sanskrit: kuśanābhasutāḥ sarvāḥ samarthās tvāṃ surottama sthānāc cyāvayituṃ devaṃ rakṣāmas tu tapo vayam
english: 'We are all daughters of Kuśanābha, O best of gods, and we are capable of casting you down from your station; but we protect our austerity.'

sanskrit: mā bhūt sa kālo durmedhaḥ pitaraṃ satyavādinam nāvamanyasva dharmeṇa svayaṃ varam upāsmahe
english: 'Let that evil time never come, O foolish one. Do not disregard our father, who is truthful. By the path of dharma we ourselves seek a husband.'

sanskrit: pitā hi prabhur asmākaṃ daivataṃ paramaṃ hi saḥ yasya no dāsyati pitā sa no bhartā bhaviṣyati
english: 'Our father is our lord and our highest deity; he to whom our father gives us shall be our husband.'

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vāyuḥ paramakopanaḥ praviśya sarvagātrāṇi babhañja bhagavān prabhuḥ
english: Hearing their words, Vāyu was filled with extreme fury; the mighty lord entered into every limb of their bodies and broke them.

sanskrit: tāḥ kanyā vāyunā bhagnā viviśur nṛpater gṛham dṛṣṭvā bhagnās tadā rājā saṃbhrānta idam abravīt
english: Broken by Vāyu, the maidens entered the palace of their father. Seeing them broken, the king was alarmed and spoke thus.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ kathyatāṃ putryaḥ ko dharmam avamanyase kubjāḥ kena kṛtāḥ sarvā veṣṭantyo nābhibhāṣatha
english: 'Tell me, O daughters, what has happened. Who has disregarded dharma? Who has made you all hunchbacked? You are writhing in pain—speak to me.'

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kuśanābhasya dhīmataḥ śirobhiś caraṇau spṛṣṭvā kanyāśatam abhāṣata
english: Hearing those words of the wise Kuśanābha, the hundred maidens touched his feet with their heads and spoke.

sanskrit: vāyuḥ sarvātmako rājan pradharṣayitum icchati aśubhaṃ mārgam āsthāya na dharmaṃ pratyavekṣate
english: 'O king, Vāyu, the all-pervading, wished to violate us; taking to an unworthy path, he did not regard dharma.'

sanskrit: pitṛmatyaḥ sma bhadraṃ te svacchande na vayaṃ sthitāḥ pitaraṃ no vṛṇīṣva tvaṃ yadi no dāsyate tava
english: 'We have a father, blessings to you; we do not stand by our own will. You choose a husband for us; let him to whom you give us take us.'

sanskrit: tena pāpānubandhena vacanaṃ na pratīcchatā evaṃ bruvantyaḥ sarvāḥ sma vāyunā nihatā bhṛṣam
english: 'Because he would not accept our words, that one bound to sin—saying thus to him, we were all severely struck down by Vāyu.'

sanskrit: tāsāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā paramadhārmikaḥ pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ kanyāśatam anuttamam
english: Hearing their words, that most righteous and greatly resplendent king replied to his hundred peerless daughters.

sanskrit: kṣāntaṃ kṣamāvatāṃ putryaḥ kartavyaṃ sumahat kṛtam aikamatyam upāgamya kulaṃ cāvekṣitaṃ mama
english: 'O daughters, forbearance is proper for those who are forbearing; you have done a very great thing. You acted in unity and have upheld the honor of my lineage.'

sanskrit: alaṃkāro hi nārīṇāṃ kṣamā tu puruṣasya vā duṣkaraṃ tac ca vaḥ kṣāntaṃ tridaśeṣu viśeṣataḥ
english: 'Forbearance is the ornament both of women and of men; and difficult indeed is the forbearance you have shown—especially toward the gods.'

sanskrit: yādṛśīr vaḥ kṣamā putryaḥ sarvāsām aviśeṣataḥ kṣamā dānaṃ kṣamā yajñaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ ca putrikāḥ
english: 'Such is the forbearance you all share equally. Forbearance is giving, forbearance is sacrifice, forbearance is truth itself, O daughters.'

sanskrit: kṣamā yaśaḥ kṣamā dharmaḥ kṣamāyāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ jagat visṛjya kanyāḥ kākutstha rājā tridaśavikramaḥ
english: 'Forbearance is glory, forbearance is dharma; the entire world rests upon forbearance.' Having dismissed the maidens, O scion of Kākutstha, that king of godlike valor—

sanskrit: mantrajño mantrayām āsa pradānaṃ saha mantribhiḥ deśe kāle pradānasya sadṛśe pratipādanam
english: —versed in counsel, deliberated with his ministers about the giving away of his daughters in marriage, discussing the proper bestowal befitting time and place.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu cūlī nāma mahāmuniḥ ūrdhvaretāḥ śubhācāro brāhmaṃ tapa upāgamat
english: At that very time a great sage named Cūlī, who had preserved his vital seed upward and was of pure conduct, was performing Brahmic austerity.

sanskrit: tapyantaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ tatra gandharvī paryupāsate somadā nāma bhadraṃ te ūrmilā tanayā tadā
english: A Gandharva woman named Somadā, daughter of Ūrmilā—blessings to you—attended upon that sage while he was performing austerity.

sanskrit: sā ca taṃ praṇatā bhūtvā śuśrūṣaṇaparāyaṇā uvāsa kāle dharmiṣṭhā tasyās tuṣṭo 'bhavad guruḥ
english: She, being devoted to his service, bowed before him and dwelt there in righteousness, season after season; the teacher became pleased with her.

sanskrit: sa ca tāṃ kālayogena provāca raghunandana parituṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te kiṃ karomi tava priyam
english: And in due time he spoke to her, O joy of the Raghu line: 'I am fully satisfied; blessings to you—what may I do that is pleasing to you?'

sanskrit: parituṣṭaṃ muniṃ jñātvā gandharvī madhurasvaram uvāca paramaprītā vākyajñā vākyakovidam
english: Knowing the sage to be fully satisfied, the Gandharva woman, sweet-voiced and skilled in speech, replied most joyfully to that master of words.

sanskrit: lakṣmyā samudito brāhmyā brahmabhūto mahātapāḥ brāhmeṇa tapasā yuktaṃ putram icchāmi dhārmikam
english: 'You are exalted with Brahmic splendor; you have become Brahman itself through great austerity. I desire a righteous son endowed with Brahmic austerity.'

sanskrit: apatiś cāsmi bhadraṃ te bhāryā cāsmi na kasya cit brāhmeṇopagatāyāś ca dātum arhasi me sutam
english: 'I have no husband, blessings to you, and I am no man's wife; since I have approached you through a Brahmic path, you ought to give me a son.'

sanskrit: tasyāḥ prasanno brahmarṣir dadau putram anuttamam brahmadatta iti khyātaṃ mānasaṃ cūlinaḥ sutam
english: The brahmin seer, pleased with her, gave her a peerless son—known as Brahmadatta, a mind-born son of Cūli.

sanskrit: sa rājā brahmadattas tu purīm adhyavasat tadā kāmpilyāṃ parayā lakṣmyā devarājo yathā divam
english: That king Brahmadatta then dwelt in the city of Kāmpilya with the highest splendor, as the king of the gods dwells in heaven.

sanskrit: sa buddhiṃ kṛtavān rājā kuśanābhaḥ sudhārmikaḥ brahmadattāya kākutstha dātuṃ kanyāśataṃ tadā
english: Then that highly righteous king Kuśanābha resolved, O scion of Kākutstha, to give his hundred daughters to Brahmadatta.

sanskrit: tam āhūya mahātejā brahmadattaṃ mahīpatiḥ dadau kanyāśataṃ rājā suprītenāntarātmanā
english: Having summoned him, the greatly resplendent king gave his hundred daughters to Brahmadatta with heartfelt joy.

sanskrit: yathākramaṃ tataḥ pāṇiṃ jagrāha raghunandana brahmadatto mahī pālas tāsāṃ devapatir yathā
english: Then in due order, O joy of the Raghu line, Brahmadatta, lord of the earth, took their hands one by one, as the lord of the gods would.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭamātre tataḥ pāṇau vikubjā vigatajvarāḥ yuktāḥ paramayā lakṣmyā babhuḥ kanyāśataṃ tadā
english: The very instant their hands were touched, all the hundred maidens became free of their hunchbacks, free of affliction, and endowed with supreme beauty.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā vāyunā muktāḥ kuśanābho mahīpatiḥ babhūva paramaprīto harṣaṃ lebhe punaḥ punaḥ
english: Seeing them released from the curse of Vāyu, the king Kuśanābha became supremely delighted and felt joy again and again.

sanskrit: kṛtodvāhaṃ tu rājānaṃ brahmadattaṃ mahīpatiḥ sadāraṃ preṣayām āsa sopādhyāya gaṇaṃ tadā
english: The king, once the marriage rites were complete, sent Brahmadatta, lord of the earth, away with his wives and together with his assembly of teachers.

sanskrit: somadāpi susaṃhṛṣṭā putrasya sadṛśīṃ kriyām yathānyāyaṃ ca gandharvī snuṣās tāḥ pratyanandata
english: And Somadā, the Gandharva woman, greatly rejoiced at her son's worthy deed and welcomed those daughters-in-law duly according to custom.

sanskrit: kṛtodvāhe gate tasmin brahmadatte ca rāghava aputraḥ putralābhāya pautrīm iṣṭim akalpayat
english: After that wedding was done and Brahmadatta had departed, O Rāghava, Kuśanābha, who was without a son, arranged the pautrī sacrifice in order to obtain a son.

sanskrit: iṣṭyāṃ tu vartamānāyāṃ kuśanābhaṃ mahīpatim uvāca paramaprītaḥ kuśo brahmasutas tadā
english: While the sacrifice was in progress, Kuśa, the son of Brahmā, greatly pleased, spoke to Kuśanābha, lord of the earth.

sanskrit: putras te sadṛśaḥ putra bhaviṣyati sudhārmikaḥ gādhiṃ prāpsyasi tena tvaṃ kīrtiṃ loke ca śāśvatīm
english: 'A son worthy of you, O son, shall be born to you, most righteous; through him you shall attain Gādhi, and through him eternal fame in the world.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā kuśo rāma kuśanābhaṃ mahīpatim jagāmākāśam āviśya brahmalokaṃ sanātanam
english: Having spoken thus to Kuśanābha, lord of the earth, O Rāma, Kuśa rose into the sky and departed to the eternal Brahmaloka.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya kuśanābhasya dhīmataḥ jajñe paramadharmiṣṭho gādhir ity eva nāmataḥ
english: Then, in the course of time, to the wise Kuśanābha was born a supremely righteous son named Gādhi.

sanskrit: sa pitā mama kākutstha gādhiḥ paramadhārmikaḥ kuśavaṃśaprasūto 'smi kauśiko raghunandana
english: 'That Gādhi, O scion of Kākutstha, supremely righteous, is my father; I am born of the lineage of Kuśa—I am Kauśika, O joy of the Raghu line.'

sanskrit: pūrvajā bhaginī cāpi mama rāghava suvratā nāmnā satyavatī nāma ṛcīke pratipāditā
english: 'My elder sister too, O Rāghava, of excellent vows, named Satyavatī, was given in marriage to Ṛcīka.'

sanskrit: saśarīrā gatā svargaṃ bhartāram anuvartinī kauśikī paramodārā sā pravṛttā mahānadī
english: 'Following her husband, she ascended to heaven in her bodily form; the most noble Kauśikī then flowed forth as a great river.'

sanskrit: divyā puṇyodakā ramyā himavantam upāśritā lokasya hitakāmārthaṃ pravṛttā bhaginī mama
english: 'Divine, of holy waters, lovely, resting upon the Himavat, my sister flows forth for the benefit and welfare of the world.'

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ himavatpārśve vasāmi niyataḥ sukham bhaginyāḥ snehasaṃyuktaḥ kauśikyā raghunandana
english: 'Therefore I dwell contentedly and happily on the slopes of Himavat, bound by affection for my sister Kauśikī, O joy of the Raghu line.'

sanskrit: sā tu satyavatī puṇyā satye dharme pratiṣṭhitā pativratā mahābhāgā kauśikī saritāṃ varā
english: 'That Satyavatī is holy, established in truth and dharma, devoted to her husband, greatly fortunate—Kauśikī, the best of rivers.'

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi niyamād rāma hitvā tāṃ samupāgataḥ siddhāśramam anuprāpya siddho 'smi tava tejasā
english: 'For I, O Rāma, have left her by vow and come hither; reaching Siddhāśrama, I have attained fulfillment through your splendor.'

sanskrit: eṣā rāma mamotpattiḥ svasya vaṃśasya kīrtitā deśasya ca mahābāho yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: 'This, O Rāma, is the account of my birth, the fame of my own lineage, and of this region, which you asked me about, O mighty-armed one.'

sanskrit: gato 'rdharātraḥ kākutstha kathāḥ kathayato mama nidrām abhyehi bhadraṃ te mā bhūd vighno 'dhvanīha naḥ
english: 'The midnight has passed while I have been telling these tales, O scion of Kākutstha. Go now to sleep; blessings to you—let there be no obstacle to us on this journey.'

sanskrit: niṣpandās taravaḥ sarve nilīnā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ naiśena tamasā vyāptā diśaś ca raghunandana
english: 'All the trees stand motionless; beasts and birds have settled to rest; the quarters are covered by the darkness of night, O joy of the Raghu line.'

sanskrit: śanair viyujyate saṃdhyā nabho netrair ivāvṛtam nakṣatratārāgahanaṃ jyotirbhir avabhāsate
english: 'The twilight glow is slowly fading; the sky is like a face covered with eyes; it glitters with the dense mass of asterisms and stars and luminaries.'

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhati ca śītāṃśuḥ śaśī lokatamonudaḥ hlādayan prāṇināṃ loke manāṃsi prabhayā vibho
english: 'The cool-rayed moon, the hare-marked one, is rising, dispelling darkness from the world, gladdening the minds of living beings everywhere with his light, O lord.'

sanskrit: naiśāni sarvabhūtāni pracaranti tatas tataḥ yakṣarākṣasasaṃghāś ca raudrāś ca piśitāśanāḥ
english: 'All creatures of the night wander here and there; companies of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, terrible and flesh-eating, roam abroad.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā virarāma mahāmuniḥ sādhu sādhv iti taṃ sarve munayo hy abhyapūjayan
english: Having spoken thus, that greatly resplendent great sage fell silent; all the sages honored him with cries of 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi saha saumitriḥ kiṃ cid āgatavismayaḥ praśasya muniśārdūlaṃ nidrāṃ samupasevate
english: Rāma too, along with Saumitri, somewhat overcome with wonder, praised that tiger among sages and then gave himself to sleep.
